answer.headline: In California multi-airport CBSAs, most measured secondary airports have a lower departure delay rate than the volume leader.
answer.body:
Passenger figures are observed T-100 enplanements ({F49.class}). Departure delay rates are calculated ({F32.class} at LAX). Gaps versus each CBSA volume leader are calculated ({F56.class}). The window is {F49.period}, the overlap of T-100 and On-Time coverage. The primary airport in each CBSA is the volume leader. The rank is the calculated gap (secondary delay rate minus the leader's delay rate), from the largest gap to the smallest. It is not an investment screen.

Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim observed enplanements were {F49}. LAX, the volume leader, had {F8}. SNA had {F24}. BUR had {F4}. LGB had {F9}.

San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont observed enplanements were {F52}. SFO, the volume leader, had {F20}. OAK had {F11}. CCR had {F5}.

San Diego-Chula Vista-Carlsbad observed enplanements were {F51}. SAN, the volume leader, had {F15}. CLD had {F6}.

Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario observed enplanements were {F50}. ONT, the volume leader, had {F12}. PSP had {F13}. SBD had {F17}.

Santa Maria-Santa Barbara observed enplanements were {F53}. SBA, the volume leader, had {F16}. SMX had {F23}.

Calculated departure delay rates for the volume leaders were LAX {F32}, SFO {F43}, SAN {F39}, ONT {F36}, and SBA {F40}.

Secondaries with a calculated delay rate, from the largest gap versus the volume leader to the smallest: PSP, SMX, SNA, OAK, BUR, LGB, CLD. There are no ties.

PSP delay rate {F37} minus ONT delay rate {F36} equals gap {F66}, a proportional difference of {F67} relative to ONT.

SMX delay rate {F46} minus SBA delay rate {F40} equals gap {F68}, a proportional difference of {F69} relative to SBA.

SNA delay rate {F47} minus LAX delay rate {F32} equals gap {F56}, a proportional difference of {F57} relative to LAX.

OAK delay rate {F35} minus SFO delay rate {F43} equals gap {F62}, a proportional difference of {F63} relative to SFO.

BUR delay rate {F29} minus LAX delay rate {F32} equals gap {F58}, a proportional difference of {F59} relative to LAX.

LGB delay rate {F33} minus LAX delay rate {F32} equals gap {F60}, a proportional difference of {F61} relative to LAX.

CLD delay rate {F30} minus SAN delay rate {F39} equals gap {F64}, a proportional difference of {F65} relative to SAN. The CLD figures carry a low On-Time coverage caveat.

CCR has no calculated departure delay rate in this window, and On-Time coverage at CCR is {F54}. SBD has no calculated departure delay rate in this window, and On-Time coverage at SBD is {F55}. CCR and SBD are omitted from the rank.

SJC is in the San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara CBSA, not the San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont CBSA, so SJC is not treated as a secondary to SFO. CBSAs with a single airport in the threshold set are outside this rank.

claims.text: Observed enplaned passengers by multi-airport CBSA are {F49} in Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim, {F52} in San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont, {F51} in San Diego-Chula Vista-Carlsbad, {F50} in Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario, and {F53} in Santa Maria-Santa Barbara.
Observed enplaned passengers in Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim are LAX {F8}, SNA {F24}, BUR {F4}, and LGB {F9}.
Observed enplaned passengers in San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont are SFO {F20}, OAK {F11}, and CCR {F5}.
Observed enplaned passengers in San Diego-Chula Vista-Carlsbad are SAN {F15} and CLD {F6}.
Observed enplaned passengers in Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario are ONT {F12}, PSP {F13}, and SBD {F17}.
Observed enplaned passengers in Santa Maria-Santa Barbara are SBA {F16} and SMX {F23}.
Calculated departure delay rates for the volume leaders are LAX {F32}, SFO {F43}, SAN {F39}, ONT {F36}, and SBA {F40}.
Calculated departure delay rates for ranked secondaries are PSP {F37}, SMX {F46}, SNA {F47}, OAK {F35}, BUR {F29}, LGB {F33}, and CLD {F30}.
Calculated gaps (secondary delay rate minus volume-leader delay rate) are PSP {F66}, SMX {F68}, SNA {F56}, OAK {F62}, BUR {F58}, LGB {F60}, and CLD {F64}.
Proportional differences versus the volume leader are PSP {F67}, SMX {F69}, SNA {F57}, OAK {F63}, BUR {F59}, LGB {F61}, and CLD {F65}.
On-Time coverage is not established at CCR ({F54}) or at SBD ({F55}), so neither airport has a departure delay rate to compare with its volume leader.
The volume leader is treated as the primary airport in each multi-airport CBSA: LAX, SFO, SAN, ONT, and SBA. That designation follows observed passenger volume, not an FAA primary-hub legal class.

Ordered by the calculated delay-rate gap versus the volume leader, from the largest gap to the smallest, the measured secondaries are PSP, SMX, SNA, OAK, BUR, LGB, and CLD, with no ties. PSP and SMX are above their leaders; the others are below.

assumptions: The primary airport in a CBSA is the member with the highest observed enplaned passengers over {F49.period}. Hub class on the airport finding labels was not the selection rule.
A multi-airport CBSA is a home CBSA with multiple California airports at or above the catalog commercial-enplanement threshold used for entity resolution. Airports below that threshold are excluded.
Geography is the airport home CBSA. Combined statistical areas are not merged, so SJC stays in San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara and is not a secondary to SFO.

The rank uses the calculated difference of departure delay rates, secondary minus volume leader. A positive gap means a higher delay rate than the leader. The proportional difference expresses that gap relative to the leader's rate.
The shared window is {F49.period}. Later On-Time months are outside it because T-100 passenger coverage does not include them.
limitations: Departure delay rates cover domestic flights of reporting carriers only. International flights and non-reporting carriers are outside the rate.
CLD delay rate {F30} and gap {F64} carry a low On-Time coverage caveat, so that comparison is a partial slice.
CCR and SBD cannot be ranked: On-Time coverage is not established, and no departure delay rate was produced.
Enplanements are T-100 segment passengers. A connecting passenger counts at each enplanement. They are not an origin-and-destination catchment total.

A CBSA is an administrative boundary, not a measured passenger catchment. Travelers cross CBSA borders, including between the San Francisco and San Jose CBSAs and between the Los Angeles and Inland Empire CBSAs.
This ordering is a delay comparison. It is not an investment screen, so there are no screening flags or scenario weights. The delay-gap order has no ties.

Unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured. A lower delay rate does not establish spare capacity, unmet demand, or an investment return. No forecast or estimated series enters this comparison.
